title: Multipath activation balancer and kernel bridge for INT8 calibration and serving
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reusable orchestration service that can run multiple INT8 calibration paths (per-layer, per-channel, and activation-transfer profiles), reconcile activation scaling factors across layers, and produce stable profiles consumable by the serving runtime. Add a thin 'kernel bridge' layer to the runtime that can switch microkernels based on profile signals and fall back gracefully for uncalibrated layers.
background: We've seen variance in INT8 accuracy when applying activation rebalancing (activation->weight scaling) across modern transformer variants, especially with KV-cache heavy workloads. Existing calibration runs produce profile blobs but there is no standardized orchestrator to evaluate multiple calibration strategies side-by-side and no lightweight runtime adapter to route execution to the best-fit microkernel. This work unifies orchestration, profiling, validation, and serving-side kernel selection.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can run at least three calibration strategies (baseline symmetric, per-channel, activation-transfer) over a given model and dataset and emit comparable profiles
Calibration outputs include per-layer scale factors and a canonical profile format accepted by the runtime bridge
Runtime kernel bridge supports at-load-time selection of optimized microkernels and a deterministic fallback when a profile is missing or flagged

End-to-end regression tests show <= 0.5% average quality delta on the validation set compared to FP32 for ResNet-style tests and <= 1.0% for large decoder-only LLMs (same datasets as runtime-1.20 eval suite)
Automated CI validates that a canary rollout (10% traffic) with the new profile does not increase 95th percentile latency by >10% or token-cost by >5%
PRD, design doc and benchmark dashboard links updated in ticket attachments
tasks: Design canonical profile schema and mapping to runtime signals (Aisha)
Implement orchestration service: job scheduling, multi-path runner, profile diff reports (Marcus)
Integrate activation-sampling harness with existing eval datastore and sample-preservation (Riley)
Implement kernel bridge in runtime: runtime hook points, microkernel registry, graceful fallback path (Marcus)
Add CI gates: regression test, latency/cost smoke, and profile format validator (SRE)
Run cluster-scale benchmarks for three representative models and publish dashboard (Bench)
Prepare rollout plan and canary config for runtime-1.22 (PM and Eng ops)
decisions: Canonical profile will be JSONL per-layer with keys: layer_id, scale_type, scale_value, confidence_score, optional microkernel_hint
Orchestrator will support running multiple calibration algorithms in parallel and produce a merged recommendation using median-of-means to reduce sampling noise
Kernel bridge will prefer microkernels tagged as 'quantized-optimized' and fallback to generic fused-op path when profile absent
We will not implement online dynamic re-scaling in this sprint; only load-time and warmup adjustments are in scope
Use existing eval datasets and add a 10k prompt holdout for stability testing rather than creating new proprietary datasets
notes: Trade-offs: running more calibration samples improves profile stability but increases calibration time and cost. We accept a longer calibration window for enterprise customers (background job) and provide a faster but noisier path for self-serve. Microkernel branching adds a small binary surface area; to mitigate risk we keep the bridge minimal and centralize registration.
